Draw the propeller shaft out of the extension housing
Plug the extension housing
expect: No oil runs out of the housing.

do: Inspect the shaft for damage and rust
Check each universal joint for play along its axes and across them
expect: None. With any play the propeller shaft assembly is replaced.

do: Measure the shaft's run-out
expect: Within the limit; beyond it the shaft is replaced.

do: Raise the front until the wheels clear the ground and support it on stands
Grip each front tyre and shake it sideways
expect: No considerable play. Play means rough bearings: adjust them (PR-096) or replace them (PR-095).

do: Raise the rear, support it on safety stands and remove the wheel and the brake drum
Mount a dial gauge and push and pull the axle shaft
expect: End play within SP-1354.

do: Raise the front, support it on stands and remove the wheel
Remove the caliper's lower attaching bolt and lift the caliper away
how: Hang the caliper from the coil spring with a piece of wire.
caution: Never let the caliper hang from the brake hose.

do: Remove the anti-rattle spring, the pads and their shims
Remove the caliper bracket
Remove the grease cap, the split pin, the nut lock and the adjusting nut
Remove the washer and the outer bearing
Remove the grease seal and the inner bearing
Drive a bearing outer race out only if it is to be replaced
how: A drift in the slots made for it.
caution: A sound outer race stays in the hub.

do: Clean the grease off both outer races with solvent and inspect them
expect: No scratches, pits or excessive wear.

do: Clean the bearings in solvent and dry them thoroughly
caution: Do not spin the bearings with compressed air.

do: Inspect the bearing rollers
expect: No damage or wear; otherwise the bearing is replaced.

do: Clean all the old grease off the spindle and out of the hub
Repack the bearings with grease
caution: Do not overpack.

do: Fill the hub cavity with the same grease
Refit the hub and bearings in the reverse order
Set the bearing preload
Tighten the adjusting nut
Turn the hub a few times to seat the bearings
Loosen the adjusting nut until it turns by hand
Hook a spring scale on a hub bolt and pull it squarely
how: Turn the hub a few times first.
expect: The pull at which the hub starts to turn is the oil seal's drag: note it.

do: Turn the adjusting nut slowly until the pull is the seal's drag plus the preload
Fit the nut lock with its slots on the spindle hole and fit a new split pin
how: If the hole does not line up, tighten the adjusting nut to the next castellation.

do: Fit the grease cap
Raise the rear and support the axle housing on stands
Remove the wheel
Remove the brake drum, the return spring and the brake shoe assembly
Remove the backing plate's attaching nuts
Remove the parking brake cable's clip and the cable
Disconnect the brake pipe
Pull the axle shaft and the backing plate out together
caution: Do not scratch the oil seal as the shaft comes out.

do: Remove the oil seal from the housing only if it is to be replaced
Fit the new oil seal into the axle housing
Grease the oil seal's lip
Refit the axle shaft assembly in the reverse order
caution: Do not damage the oil seal's lip.

do: Bleed the brake line
Remove the axle shaft
Grind one part of the bearing collar down to a thin wall
caution: Keep the grinder off the shaft.

do: Break that part with a chisel and take the collar off the shaft
caution: Do not mark the shaft with the chisel.

do: Support the spacer and press the axle shaft out of the bearing
Inspect the axle shaft for bend, cracks and worn splines
how: Deflection limit at the centre: SP-1401.

do: Inspect the back plate
expect: Not deformed, cracked or damaged.

do: Check the bearing's play and rotation
how: Turn it while pressing from the centre outward.
caution: Do not clean the bearing with gasoline.

do: Check the oil seal's lip
expect: Not worn or damaged.

do: Press the bearing onto the shaft
how: The back plate goes on the shaft first. Attachment SP-1675.

do: Clean the new collar and its seat on the shaft with clean rags
caution: No oil or grease on the collar or the shaft.

do: Press the new collar onto the shaft
expect: The press-fit force is above SP-1402; at that figure or under it, the collar or the shaft is replaced.

do: Raise the rear and support it on safety stands
Drain the differential oil
Pull both rear axle shafts
Remove the propeller shaft
Undo the carrier's fasteners, leaving two on loosely
how: The two keep the differential from dropping.

do: Free the carrier with a wooden hammer and lift the differential out
Refit in the reverse order with sealant on the joint
Bleed the brake line
Fill with differential oil
Mount the rear axle assembly on the engine stand
Mark one of the bearing caps
how: So left and right go back on their own sides.

do: Remove the adjuster lock plates
Remove the bearing caps and the adjusters
Lift out the differential assembly and its bearings
caution: Keep each bearing outer race with its own bearing.

do: Hold the companion flange and remove the drive pinion nut
Pull the companion flange off
Take the drive pinion out of the carrier with its spacer, rear bearing and collapsible spacer
Remove the oil seal and the front bearing
Drive the bearing outer races out only if needed
how: A drift in the slots made for it.

do: Pull the side bearings off the gear case
Remove the ring gear
Drive the pinion shaft's lock pin out with a drift
Remove the pinion shaft, the pinion gears, then the side gears and their thrust washers
Wash the parts and inspect the drive pinion and the ring gear
how: They are replaced only as a set.
expect: Teeth not damaged, worn or chipped; bearing journals and splines sound.

do: Inspect the side gears and the pinion gears
expect: No cracks or chipped teeth.

do: Inspect the differential bearings and the pinion bearings
expect: No wear or flaking.

do: Measure the collapsible spacer's length with a micrometer
Inspect the oil seal and the companion flange
expect: Seal not worn; flange not cracked, its splines not worn and its seal surface smooth.

do: Check the bearing bores of the carrier are free of dirt and burrs
Fit the front and rear bearing races into the carrier
Put the spacer, the rear bearing and collar B on the pinion model and hold them with the O-ring
caution: The model's head screws in: check it is not loose.

do: Fit them in the carrier
caution: Never use the collapsible spacer for this measurement.

do: Fit the front bearing, collar A, the companion flange and the washer
Tighten the nut until the pinion model turns smoothly
Zero a dial indicator in the gauge body on a surface plate
Put the gauge block on the pinion model and the gauge body on the block
Read the lowest point of each side bearing seat in the carrier, left and right
Work out the adjustment value and choose the spacer
Put the chosen spacer on the drive pinion and press the rear bearing on
Fit the collapsible spacer on the pinion and put them in the carrier
Fit the front bearing on the pinion's front end
Oil the pinion oil seal's lip with gear oil and fit the seal in the carrier
Tap the companion flange onto the pinion with a plastic hammer
Fit the washer and nut and, before tightening, measure the oil seal's drag with a torque wrench
Tighten the pinion nut to the first figure and check the preload
how: SP-1406. A little at a time, with the preload checked after each.
caution: Never beyond SP-1407; if the preload is not reached at that torque, fit a new collapsible spacer.

do: Set the preload
how: SP-1416, the seal's drag of step 6 not counted. With a spring scale at the flange's bolt hole: SP-1408.

do: Put a thrust washer on each side gear and fit the gears in the gear case
Insert the two pinion gears through the case's openings, exactly opposite each other
Turn the gears 90 degrees until their holes line up with the case's pinion shaft holes
Push the pinion shaft through the case and the pinion gears
Check the backlash of the side gears and pinion gears
how: Set by the thrust washers' thickness, SP-1419.

do: Fit the pinion shaft's lock pin and stake it with a punch
Apply locking agent to the back of the ring gear and to its bolts
how: Where the figure shows; it was not read.

do: Fit the ring gear to the case and torque its bolts
Press the side bearings onto the gear case
expect: Pressed until the force rises suddenly.

do: Put the differential gear assembly in the carrier
Fit each adjuster on its own side, by its mark
Fit the bearing caps by their marks and start their bolts
Nip one bearing cap bolt on each side
Mark the ring gear at four points about 90 degrees apart and set a dial indicator square on a tooth
Turn both adjusters equally until the backlash is right
Check the backlash at the other three marks
expect: Smallest reading above SP-1410; spread within SP-1411.

do: Tighten the adjusters equally until the bearing caps' pilots are the set distance apart
caution: Do not disturb the backlash.

do: Torque the bearing cap bolts
Fit the adjuster lock plates on the bearing caps
Coat both faces of six to eight ring gear teeth thinly and evenly with red lead
Rock the ring gear by hand while turning the drive pinion several times
Read the contact pattern on the teeth
expect: Good contact as the page's figures show it; they were not read.

do: Wipe the red lead off if the contact is good
With toe or flank contact, fit a thinner pinion spacer
how: The pinion moves outward. Then set the backlash again, PR-104.

do: With heel or face contact, fit a thicker pinion spacer
how: The pinion moves inward. Then set the backlash again, PR-104.

do: Set the front wheels straight ahead
Turn the steering wheel slowly and measure at its rim how far it moves before the front wheels begin to move
expect: Within SP-109; the limit is SP-1424.

do: With excessive play, check four places
how: The centre link's ball joints, the idler arm's bushes (PR-110), the wheel bearings (PR-094), and the backlash between sector shaft and ball nut (PR-107 step 16).

do: Disconnect the battery's negative cable
Mark the steering wheel and the column shaft, then remove the horn cap and pull the steering wheel
caution: Never strike the column shaft's end with a hammer: it damages the bearing or the collapsible shaft.

do: Remove the steering column covers
Remove the air duct and disconnect the combination switch's couplers
Remove the combination switch assembly
Remove the steering lock assembly
Remove the column jacket's fixing bracket
Mark the hinge positions on the bonnet and remove the bonnet
Raise the front and support it on stands
Disconnect the centre link from the pitman arm
Pull the pitman arm off the sector shaft
Remove the steering gear housing's bolts and lift the assembly out through the engine compartment
caution: After a collision, check the steering wheel for axial play first: with a crushed column shaft or axial play, the gear and column shaft are replaced as an assembly.

do: Refit in the reverse order, with the shim back in its place between the housing and the frame
how: The shim sets the column shaft's alignment. Housing bolts SP-1432.

do: Fit the pitman arm on the sector shaft with their matching serrations aligned and torque the nut
Turn the sector shaft through its travel several times from the pitman arm and stop the arm at the centre
expect: It turns smoothly.

do: Set a dial indicator on the pitman arm's end and turn the adjusting screw until the backlash at the centre is right, then tighten its lock nut
Measure the worm shaft preload at the centre of its travel, the centre link off the pitman arm
how: Attachment SP-1446 on the column shaft's end.
expect: The with-sector-shaft figure of SP-1690 (as a torque, SP-1427).

do: Fit the steering wheel with its marks aligned
Fill the gear housing with oil
how: Oil SP-252; the 1985 quantity is SP-1689.

do: Drain the oil
Hold the gear housing in a vice or on the engine stand
Slide the column jacket off the column shaft
Loosen the adjusting cover's lock nut
Remove the side cover's bolts
Tap the sector shaft assembly out of the housing with a plastic hammer
caution: Do not damage the shaft.

do: Unscrew the end cover's lock nut and loosen the end cover
Take out the worm shaft and ball nut assembly
caution: Do not take the worm shaft and ball nut apart.

do: Remove the oil seal only if it must be replaced
Run the ball nut along the worm shaft
expect: It travels smoothly and freely; with any roughness the steering gear assembly is replaced.

do: Check the worm bearings and their cups
expect: No wear or damage; otherwise the steering gear assembly is replaced.

do: Twirl the sector shaft's tapered roller bearing under a thrust load
expect: No catching and no abnormal sound; otherwise the sector shaft assembly is replaced.

do: Check the oil seal
expect: No wear, flaw or damage; replace it if it could leak.

do: Fit the oil seal if it was removed
caution: Never tap the oil seal directly with a hammer.

do: Fit the worm shaft and ball nut assembly in the housing
Screw the end cover in until the worm shaft's preload is right
how: A spring scale pulled squarely on attachment SP-1446 at the column shaft's end, read as the shaft starts to turn.
expect: The without-sector-shaft figure of SP-1690 (as a torque, SP-1426).

do: Tighten the end cover's lock nut and check the preload again
Turn the worm shaft until the rack is at the centre of the worm
Fit the sector shaft assembly with the centre of its gear on the centre of the rack
caution: Do not damage the oil seal.

do: Put sealing agent on the side cover, place it on the sector shaft assembly and turn the sector shaft counter-clockwise until the cover is screwed into place
Torque the side cover's bolts
Nip the adjusting cover's lock nut
Turn the adjusting cover clockwise with a punch and hammer until the gear's preload is right
expect: The with-sector-shaft figure of SP-1690 (as a torque, SP-1427).

do: Torque the adjusting cover's lock nut
Fit the column jacket onto the end cover
Raise the front and support it on stands
Disconnect the centre link from the idler arm
Remove the idler arm assembly from the frame
Hold the assembly in a vice and remove the split pin, nut and washer
Take the idler arm and its bushes off the bracket
Check the bushes
expect: Not excessively worn; otherwise they are replaced.

do: Put a bush on the idler arm's spindle and grease bush and spindle
Fit the idler arm to the bracket and pack grease into the bracket
Fit the other bush and the washer
Tighten the spindle nut and fit a new split pin
Check the idler arm's revolving torque with a spring scale
expect: SP-1443; outside it the bushes are replaced.

do: Fit the assembly to the frame and torque its bolts
Connect the centre link to the idler arm, torque the nut and fit a new split pin
Inspect the ball joint for wear
expect: A worn joint is replaced whole. The joints are sealed with lithium grease and are not lubricated in service.

do: Check the dust seal
expect: No wear, flaw or damage.

do: To replace the dust seal, remove the ball joint, hold it in a vice and take the seal off
Pack a little grease into the new dust seal and press it on
Raise the front and support it on stands
Disconnect the centre link from the pitman arm
Loosen the nut and pull the pitman arm off the sector shaft
Fit the pitman arm on the sector shaft with their matching serrations aligned and torque the nut
Connect the centre link to the pitman arm, torque the nut and fit a new split pin
Raise the front, support it on stands and remove the front wheel
Disconnect the tie-rod from the centre link and from the knuckle arm
Fit the tie-rod to the centre link and the knuckle arm
Torque the nuts and fit new split pins
Reset the toe-in
caution: The toe-in is reset whenever a tie-rod or a ball joint is replaced.

do: Raise the front and support it on stands
Disconnect the centre link from both tie-rods, the pitman arm and the idler arm
Fit the centre link to the pitman arm, the idler arm and the tie-rods
Torque the nuts and fit new split pins
how: Idler arm SP-1437; pitman arm SP-1436; tie-rods SP-1438.

do: Set the tyre pressures
Check the front wheel bearing play and correct it
Check the wheels and tyres for run-out and balance
Check the ball joints of the front suspension and the steering linkage for looseness
Stand the car on level ground with no luggage and nobody in it
Raise the front until the wheels clear the ground
Turn each wheel by hand and scribe a line round the centre of its tread
Lower the car and set the front wheels straight ahead
Measure between the lines at the front and at the rear of the wheels, at the same height from the ground
expect: The rear measurement is larger than the front by SP-102.

do: If the toe-in is wrong, turn both tie-rods by equal amounts
Measure camber and caster with a wheel aligning gauge, by its maker's instructions
expect: SP-103 and SP-104.

do: If they are wrong, raise the front on stands and open the bonnet
Remove the four nuts holding the front suspension mounting block to the fender apron
Press the suspension down and turn the mounting block to the position that gives the change needed
Torque the mounting block's nuts
Lower the car and check camber and caster again
expect: If they still cannot be set, the front suspension and the body alignment are checked and repaired.

do: Set the steering angle with the adjusting bolt on each steering knuckle arm
expect: SP-1430 inward, SP-1431 outward.

do: Disconnect the battery's negative cable
Remove the horn cap
Mark the steering wheel and the column shaft and pull the steering wheel
caution: Never strike the column shaft's end with a hammer: it damages the bearing or the collapsible shaft.

do: Remove the steering column covers
Remove the air duct and disconnect the combination switch's couplers
Remove the combination switch assembly
Put a protector under the steering lock assembly
how: It keeps the hammer blows off the steering shaft.

do: Loosen the bolts holding the lock body to the column jacket with a chisel
Position the new steering lock on the column jacket and tighten its bolts
expect: The bolt heads snap off.

do: Refit the combination switch, the column covers and the steering wheel in the reverse order
Raise the front, support it on stands and remove the front wheel
Remove the caliper's lower attaching bolt and lift the lower side of the caliper
Remove the anti-rattle spring, then the pads and their shims
Measure the lining's thickness
expect: Above the limit of SP-1365; at it the pad is replaced.
caution: Replace all the pads on both wheels together and never mix types of pad.

do: Fit the pads in the reverse order
how: Coat the caliper's mounting pin and attaching bolt with the grease from the pad kit.

do: If the caliper will not go over the new pads, take the cap off the bleeder screw and run a vinyl tube from it into a container
Loosen the bleeder screw and press the piston into the cylinder
Tighten the bleeder screw, remove the tube and the tool, and fit the caliper
Raise the front, support it on stands and remove the front wheel
Loosen the flexible hose at the caliper without removing it
Remove the caliper's lower attaching bolt and lift the caliper up
Slide the caliper toward the inside of the car and off
Disconnect the flexible hose from the caliper and plug its end
Clean the outside of the caliper
Remove the dust boot's retainer and the dust boot
Put a hardwood block in the caliper and blow compressed air gradually into the fluid hole until the piston comes out
how: If it sticks, tap lightly round the piston while the air is on.

do: Remove the piston seal, then the bleeder cap and screw
Clean the parts in clean brake fluid or alcohol and blow them dry
caution: Never gasoline or kerosene.

do: Inspect the caliper bore and the piston
expect: No scoring, scratches or rust. Minor damage is polished out with crocus cloth; otherwise the piston or the caliper is replaced.

do: Assemble in the reverse order with a new piston seal and a new dust seal
how: The seal kit's two greases, orange and red, go where the page's figure shows; it was not read. Brake fluid on the piston and the bore.
expect: The piston seal sits fully in its groove, not twisted.

do: Refit the caliper in the reverse order and connect the hose
Bleed the brakes
Set the front wheel bearing preload first
Remove the pads and the caliper
Inspect the disc's surfaces and measure its thickness
expect: No scoring, scratches, rust or excessive wear; reface it as necessary, down to the limit.

do: Measure the lateral run-out with a dial indicator
expect: Within the run-out limit of SP-113.

do: To replace the disc, remove the hub
Raise the rear, support the axle housing on stands and remove the rear wheel
Remove the brake drum's attaching screws
Release the parking brake fully and remove the drum
Remove the return springs
Remove the shoes' retaining springs and guide pins
Remove the brake shoes and the adjuster strut
Unhook the parking brake cable from the operating lever on the shoe
Inspect the drum for damage, wear and scores and measure its inner diameter
expect: SP-115; roughness within SP-1353.

do: Inspect the linings for wear, damage and deformation and measure their thickness
expect: Standard SP-1350; the limit is in SP-115.

do: Look at the wheel cylinder's boots
expect: Dry. A boot wet with brake fluid means the wheel cylinder is overhauled, PR-121.

do: Inspect the brake lines, pipes, hoses and connections
expect: No leaks, chafing, deterioration or damage.

do: Refit the shoes in the reverse order
how: Multi-purpose grease where a shoe touches the backing plate, the wheel cylinder's piston and the anchor pin.

do: Adjust the rear brakes
Remove the rear brake shoes
Disconnect the brake pipe at the wheel cylinder and plug the pipe
Remove the wheel cylinder from the backing plate
Take the cylinder apart: dust boots, pistons, piston cups, filling blocks, spring, bleeder cap and screw, steel ball
Wash every part in clean alcohol or brake fluid
caution: Never gasoline or kerosene.

do: Examine the bore and the pistons for wear, roughness and scoring and measure the clearance between them
expect: Within SP-1356; beyond SP-1357 the cylinder or the piston is replaced.

do: Inspect the piston cups
expect: No wear, softening, swelling or damage; otherwise new cups.

do: Assemble and refit in the reverse order
how: Union SP-1359. Multi-purpose grease where a shoe touches the backing plate, the wheel cylinder's piston and the anchor pin.

do: Bleed the brakes and check that they work properly
Raise the rear until the wheels turn freely and support it on stands
Release the parking brake fully
Take the adjusting hole plugs out of the back of the backing plate
With a screwdriver in hole A, turn the star wheel the way the arrow on the backing plate points until the wheel locks
Push the adjuster lever with the screwdriver through hole B and back the star wheel off
expect: The wheel turns freely without drag.

do: Fit the adjusting hole plugs
Do the same on the other rear wheel
Disconnect the fluid level sensor's coupler
Disconnect the fluid pipes at the master cylinder's outlets
caution: Never let brake fluid drop on a painted surface.

do: Remove the proportioning bypass valve's attaching bolt
Remove the master cylinder assembly

Drain the fluid and take the cylinder apart in order: reservoir set, bushes, joint bolt with check valve and spring, secondary piston stop bolt and O-ring, stop ring, primary piston assembly, secondary piston assembly and spring
Wash the parts in clean alcohol or brake fluid and blow them dry
caution: Never gasoline or kerosene.

do: Check the piston cups
expect: Not damaged, worn, softened or swollen; otherwise new cups.

do: Examine the bore and the pistons for wear, roughness and scoring and measure the clearance between them
expect: Within SP-1339; beyond SP-1340 the cylinder or the piston is replaced.

do: Check the compensating ports of the cylinder are open
Dip the pistons and cups in clean brake fluid and fit the secondary and primary cups to the pistons
how: The cups' directions are in the page's figure; it was not read.

do: Fit the check valve with its face, the side with the six holes, toward the cylinder body, and torque the joint bolt
how: SP-1342 (the page gives the same as 6.0-7.0 m-kg). The check valve is the rear drum brake car's.

do: Assemble the rest in the reverse order and, before the reservoir goes on, look into the ports
expect: The piston cups do not cover the compensating ports.

do: Refit the master cylinder in the reverse order of removal
Bleed the brakes and check that they work properly
Engine stopped, press the pedal several times; hold it down and start the engine
expect: The pedal moves down very slightly just after the engine starts.

do: Run the engine for one or two minutes, stop it, then press the pedal several times with normal force
expect: The stroke is long the first time and shorter each time after. If not, check the check valve and the vacuum hoses for damage or wrong fitting, repair, and repeat.

do: Start the engine, press the pedal with normal force, stop the engine with the pedal held, and hold it for about 30 seconds
expect: The pedal's height does not change.

do: If the fault is still not found, connect a pressure gauge, a vacuum gauge and a pedal force gauge and bleed the pressure gauge
how: As the page's figure shows; it was not read.

do: Start the engine, stop it when the vacuum reaches the test figure, and time the vacuum's fall with no load on the pedal
Repeat with the pedal held at the test force
Engine stopped and no vacuum, read the fluid pressure at the test pedal force
Engine running and the vacuum at the test figure, read the fluid pressure at the same pedal force
Remove the vacuum hose with its check valve and blow through it from each end
expect: Air passes from the power brake unit's end to the engine's end and not the other way. A faulty valve is replaced with its hose.
caution: The arrow on the hose shows the direction it is fitted.

do: Remove the brake master cylinder
Disconnect the vacuum hose at the power brake unit
Disconnect the push rod's fork from the brake pedal
Remove the power brake unit
Put mating marks on the rear shell and the front shell
Remove the fork end and its lock nut, then the dust boot
With a wrench on the rear shell's studs, press the rear shell down and turn it clockwise to the unlocked position, then lift it off
caution: The shell is spring-loaded: loosen it carefully.

do: Remove the spring
Remove the air silencer's retainer, then the power piston with the valve rod and plunger assembly from the rear shell
Remove the diaphragm
Press the valve rod in and take out the valve retainer key, then the valve rod and plunger assembly
caution: The valve rod and plunger are serviced only as an assembly.

do: Remove the air silencer and its filter, then the reaction disc
Remove the retainer, the bearing and the rear seal from the rear shell
caution: Leave the rear seal in the shell unless it is defective and a new one is to hand.

do: Remove the push rod, the retainer, then the front seal and the support plate
caution: Leave the front seal in the shell unless it is defective and a new one is to hand.

do: Inspect all the rubber parts and the diaphragm
expect: No cuts, nicks or other damage.

do: Check the power piston and the reaction disc
expect: Piston not cracked, distorted or chipped, its seats sound; disc not deteriorated.

do: Check the valve rod and plunger and both shells
expect: Seats smooth, no nicks or dents; shells free of scratches, scores, pits and dents.

do: Assemble in the reverse order with the repair kit's silicone grease
how: On the valve rod and plunger assembly's surfaces, the whole reaction disc, the diaphragm's outer bead and the lips of the front and rear seals.

do: Fit the valve retainer key
how: Press the valve rod down until its groove lines up with the slot of the power piston.

do: Fit the rear shell assembly on the front shell and turn it counter-clockwise with the wrench until the mating marks line up
caution: Keep the shell pressed down firmly until the flanges are fully locked.

do: Set the adjust gauge on the master cylinder and drive its screw in until it touches the cylinder's piston
Turn the gauge over onto the power brake unit and turn the push rod until there is no clearance between it and the gauge's screw head
expect: The push rod to piston clearance is then SP-1697.

do: Refit the power brake unit and the master cylinder in the reverse order
Raise the car and support it on stands
Take the rubber cap off a bleeder screw, fit a vinyl tube to it and put the tube's end under brake fluid in a glass jar
Loosen the bleeder screw, press the pedal its full stroke and let it return slowly; go on until no bubbles come out
caution: Keep the reservoir filled, SP-1698.

do: Tighten the bleeder screw, remove the tube and fit the cap
Bleed the other system the same way
how: The front and rear hydraulic systems are bled separately.

do: Fill the reservoir and fit its cap
caution: Never use again fluid that was drained from the system.

do: Disconnect the wires from the stop light switch
Loosen the lock nut and turn the stop light switch until the pedal height is right
Tighten the lock nut and connect the switch's wires
Loosen the push rod's lock nut and turn the push rod at the pedal until the free travel is right
Tighten the lock nut
Check the parking brake is fully released
Raise the rear until the wheels turn freely and support it on stands
Turn the lever's adjusting screw until the rear brakes lock at the right number of notches
how: SP-1386 at the pull of SP-1387.

do: Apply the parking brake several times, release it and turn the rear wheels
expect: They turn freely without dragging.

do: Lower the car
Set the parking brake warning light switch
expect: The light comes on with the lever pulled one notch and goes out with it fully released.

do: Disconnect the fluid pipes at the proportioning bypass valve
caution: Never let brake fluid drop on a painted surface.

do: Remove the valve and fit the new one
Connect the fluid pipes by the identification marks on the valve body
Bleed the brakes
With the foot brake applied, inspect every brake line for leaks
expect: None.

do: Check every pipe, hose and connection
expect: No chafing, deterioration or other damage.

do: Raise the front and support it on stands
Remove the wheel hub assembly from the shock absorber
Remove the backing plate
Remove the flexible hose's attaching clip
Remove the bolts holding the knuckle arm to the shock absorber
Note where the triangle mark on the mounting block sits, then remove the block's nuts and take the shock absorber assembly out
caution: The mark's position is needed at refitting: it sets camber and caster.

do: Hold the mounting block in a vice and loosen the lock nut a few turns
caution: Do not remove the lock nut yet.

do: Compress the coil spring
Take off in order: lock nut and washer, mounting block and adjusting plate, seat, thrust bearing, spring upper seat, coil spring, dust boot, bound bumper
Hold the shock absorber upright and work the piston rod through its full travel four or five times
expect: Strong hydraulic resistance. No resistance, or a sudden free movement, means the shock absorber is repaired.

do: Look for fluid on the outside
expect: None in excess; otherwise the shock absorber is repaired.

do: Clamp the reservoir tube in a vice with soft jaws
Remove the cap nut and seal assembly from the reservoir tube
Remove the O-ring from the piston rod guide
Pull the piston rod and pressure tube assembly out of the reservoir tube
caution: Do not take the base valve off the pressure tube or the piston off the rod.

do: Inspect the reservoir tube and the mounting block
expect: No deformation, cracks, deterioration or damage.

do: Turn the mounting bearing
expect: No slackness and no abnormal noise.

do: Inspect the coil spring
expect: No signs of fatigue, cracks or damage.

do: Inspect the cap nut's threads and the oil seal's lip
expect: Threads sound, lip not worn or damaged.

do: Fill the reservoir tube with shock absorber fluid
how: SP-1462. Steps 11 to 15 are not needed with a cartridge type damper.

do: Put the pilot over the piston rod's threads
Grease the oil seal's lip and pass the new cap nut over the pilot onto the piston rod
caution: The cap nut and oil seal assembly is always a new one.

do: With the piston rod fully extended, nip the cap nut
Lower the piston rod fully and torque the cap nut
With a cartridge type damper, torque its cap nut instead
Assemble the spring and the upper parts on the shock absorber in the reverse order
how: A thin coat of rubber grease on both sides of the thrust bearing. Piston rod to mounting block SP-1470.
expect: The lower end of the coil spring butts against the shoulder formed in the spring seat.

do: Fit the mounting block to the car with its triangle mark where it was
caution: If the mounting block was replaced, the wheel alignment is adjusted, PR-115.

do: Bolt the knuckle arm to the shock absorber
how: SP-1475; the 1985 page's figure is SP-1705.

do: Refit the backing plate, the caliper adaptor and the hub
Set the front wheel bearing preload
On level ground, measure from the ground to each headlamp
expect: The two sides differ by no more than SP-1472.

do: If they differ by more, fit an adjusting plate between the mounting block and the suspension tower
caution: No more than SP-1708 on one side.

do: Raise the front, support it on stands and remove the front wheel
Remove the bolts holding the knuckle arm to the steering knuckle
Disconnect the tie-rod end
Disconnect the stabilizer bar and the tension rod from the arm
Disconnect the knuckle arm from the ball joint
Remove the suspension arm's attaching bolt and the arm
Inspect the arm and its bushing, the ball joint's dust boot and the knuckle arm
expect: No deformation, cracks, wear, flaws or damage.

do: Hold the arm in a vice, fit the knuckle arm to the ball joint and turn the ball stud a few turns to settle it
Hook a spring scale in the knuckle arm's tie-rod hole, steady the arm with a finger and pull
expect: At least SP-1503; under it the whole arm is replaced.
caution: The arm and its ball joint do not come apart: either one defective means a new assembly.

do: To replace the arm's bushing, press the old one out toward the front and the new one in from the front
caution: No lubricant on the bushing or in the arm's bore.

do: To replace the ball joint's dust boot, take the old one off, fill the new one with lithium grease and press it on
Refit the arm in the reverse order with its cross member bolt only lightly tightened
how: Ball joint to knuckle arm SP-1502; tension rod SP-1504; knuckle arm to shock absorber SP-1475. The 1985 page's figure for the first and last is SP-1705.

do: Fit the stabilizer bar to the arm and set its nut
Lower the car, bounce it a few times to settle the suspension, then torque the arm's cross member bolt
Raise the front and support it on stands
Remove the engine under cover
Remove the tension rods' attaching nuts and the tension rods
Disconnect both ends of the stabilizer bar from the right and left control links
Remove the stabilizer bar's support plates and rubber bushings
Remove the right and left brackets that carry the tension rods and the stabilizer bar, with the bar
Inspect the removed parts
expect: No cracks, deformation, damage or weakness.

do: Fit the brackets to the frame with the stabilizer bar and torque their bolts
Fit both ends of the stabilizer bar to the control links and set the nuts
Fit the stabilizer's rubber bushings and support plates with each bushing's open end toward the front, bolts only nipped
Fit each tension rod's front end to its bracket, set nut A, then torque nut B
how: Nut A SP-1506; nut B SP-1505. The flat face of the rubber bushing goes toward the bracket.

do: Fit each tension rod's rear end to the suspension arm and torque its nuts
Lower the car, bounce it a few times, then torque the stabilizer's support plates
Raise the rear and support it under the lower link brackets, front side, on stands
Remove the rear wheel
Remove the side trim in the luggage compartment and undo the shock absorber's upper end
Undo the lower end and take the shock absorber out
Inspect the shock absorber
expect: Works, quiet, no fluid leak, bushings not worn; otherwise it is replaced.

do: Fit the shock absorber and torque its lower end
how: SP-1482. On the left side the lower bolt goes in with its head toward the inside.

do: Tighten the upper nut to its setting
Raise the rear and support it under the lower link brackets, front sides, on stands; take the rear axle casing's weight on a jack
Remove the rear wheels
Disconnect from the axle casing: the shock absorbers' lower ends, the lower links' rear ends, the upper links' rear ends, the stabilizer bar's front ends, and both Watt links
Lower the axle casing carefully on the jack and take out the coil springs and their rubber seats
Check each coil spring
expect: No cracks or damage; otherwise a new spring.

do: Fit each spring with its painted mark toward the rear axle casing
Reconnect the links, the shock absorbers' lower ends and the Watt links with their bolts and nuts only nipped
how: On the left side the shock absorber's lower bolt goes in with its head toward the inside.

do: Fit the stabilizer bar's ends and set their nuts
how: SP-1498 (the page points at 13-12, the front bar's figure; the rear bar's is on 13-17).

do: Lower the car and torque everything that was nipped
how: Links SP-1488, SP-1490; Watt links SP-1493; shock absorbers SP-1482.

do: Raise the rear and support it under the lower link brackets, front sides, on stands; take the rear axle casing's weight on a jack
Disconnect the right Watt link, then the left one, from the body frame
Remove the Watt link bracket's attaching nut and take the bracket off with both links
Take each link off the bracket
Inspect the removed parts
expect: No cracks, deformation or damage.

do: Refit in the reverse order, each link with its painted mark toward the front and the outside, everything only nipped
Lower the car and torque the links and the bracket
how: Links at both ends SP-1493, SP-1494; bracket to axle casing SP-1492.

do: Raise the rear and support it under the lower link brackets, front sides, on stands; take the rear axle casing's weight on a jack
Disconnect both ends of the stabilizer bar
Remove the bar's mounting brackets if necessary
Remove the support plates and rubber bushings, then the bar
Inspect the removed parts
expect: No cracks, deformation or damage.

do: Fit the rubber bushings and support plates with each bushing's open end toward the rear, bolts only nipped
Fit both ends of the bar to their brackets and set the nuts
how: SP-1498, then SP-1497. Mounting brackets to the body frame SP-1499.

do: Lower the car and torque the support plates
Raise the rear and support it under the lower link brackets, front side, on stands; take the rear axle casing's weight on a jack
Remove the rear wheel
Remove the links' bolts and nuts and take the upper and lower links off
Inspect the links
expect: No cracks, deformation or damage.

do: Fit the links with their bolts and nuts only nipped
how: The upper link's rear bolt goes in with its head toward the inside.

do: Lower the car and torque the links' bolts and nuts
Work each seat's adjuster lever and reclining knuckle
expect: They move smoothly; the adjustment lever is not worn.

do: Check the front seats' mounting bolts
expect: None loose.

do: To replace a seat belt, remove the rear floor mat and the floor plate
Remove the seat belt's anchor bolt and the bolt holding the retractor
Take out the seat belt and retractor assembly
caution: Do not take a retractor apart.

do: Fit the new assembly in the reverse order
expect: The retractor sits vertical when its bolt is tightened.

do: Open the hood and mark the hinge positions on it
Remove the hood stay
With an assistant holding one side, remove the hood's mounting bolts and lift the hood off
Refit in the reverse order
Loosen the hood's mounting bolts and move it fore and aft, side to side and up and down until it fits
Loosen the hood lock's bolts and move the lock until it lines up with the striker
Remove the battery
Disconnect the connectors of the front turn signal lights
Remove the nuts holding the piston rod end of each bumper shock absorber to the body
Raise the front and support it on stands
Remove the radiator grille
Remove the bolts holding the shock absorber brackets to the frame and take off brackets, shock absorbers and bumper together
Unbolt the shock absorbers from the bumper
Measure each shock absorber
how: Length A SP-1260; length B, set by moving the bracket, SP-1261.
expect: A within its figure; otherwise a new shock absorber.

do: Refit in the reverse order
caution: The bumper face is urethane: do not damage it.

do: Check the bumper's height with no load, the tyres at their pressure and a full fuel tank
Open the rear glass hatch and remove the service hole cover
Remove the nuts holding the piston rod end of each bumper shock absorber to the frame
Raise the rear and support it on stands
Remove the nuts holding the shock absorber brackets to the frame and take off brackets, shock absorbers and bumper together
Unbolt the shock absorbers from the bumper
Measure each shock absorber
how: Length A SP-1265; length B, set by moving the bracket, SP-1266.
expect: A within its figure; otherwise a new shock absorber.

do: Refit in the reverse order
caution: The bumper face is urethane: do not damage it.

do: Check the bumper's height with no load, the tyres at their pressure and a full fuel tank
Loosen the striker's screws and move the striker in or out, up or down
Tighten the screws and check how the door fits
For the glass's level, raise the window fully and move the regulator guide up or down
expect: The glass moves smoothly.

do: For its fore and aft position, loosen the adjusting bolt, move the glass guide and tighten the bolt
expect: The glass has no play back and forth.

do: Remove the regulator handle, the inner handle cover and the arm rest
Remove the trim panel
Remove the inner handle assembly and the watershield
Remove the screws holding the glass to the regulator, then the screw grommets
Remove the glass
Remove the regulator's bolts and take the regulator out through the service hole
Power window type only: remove the motor's mounting bolts and take the motor off the regulator
caution: The spring is released as the motor comes off and the regulator gear snaps back to the up position.

do: Refit in the reverse order and adjust the regulator if necessary
how: PR-144. Power window type: before the motor goes on, run the regulator down on a battery to the position the page's figure shows; it was not read.

do: Raise the glass fully and remove the regulator handle, the arm rest and the inner handle cover
Remove the trim panel
Remove the inner handle's bolts, disconnect the remote control rod at the door lock and take the inner handle out
Pry the watershield away carefully
Disconnect the push rod at the door lock and remove it
Disconnect the rod at the key cylinder, remove the clip and take the key cylinder out
Disconnect the rod at the outer handle, remove the handle's nuts and take the outer handle off
Remove the door lock's screws and take the lock out through the service hole
Refit in the reverse order with a new nylon bush on the outer handle
Adjust the inner handle to its proper play
Open the rear glass hatch and disconnect the battery's negative cable
Remove the weatherstrip and the top ceiling at the rear end of the roof
Disconnect the rear defroster's connector at the rear pillar
Remove the rear side pillar trim
Disconnect the damper stays at the body and close the hatch
caution: Do not damage the defroster filament on the glass.

do: Remove the hinges' attaching nuts
Release the hatch lock and lift the hatch off with its hinges
If necessary, take the damper stays, the hinges and the lock striker off the glass
how: Before a stay is discarded, drill its cylinder's lower end, SP-1226, to let the gas out.
caution: Never take a damper stay apart: it holds gas and oil. Cuttings and oil can fly out hard as it is drilled.

do: Refit in the reverse order
To adjust the lock, loosen its bolts and move it until it lines up with the hatch's striker
To adjust the hinges, open the hatch and remove the upper part of the weatherstrip, the rear end of the top ceiling and the rear header pads
Close the hatch, loosen the hinges' nuts, move the hatch until it lines up with the body and tighten the nuts
Remove the rear view mirror and the sun visors
Remove the seaming welts, the front pillar trims and the rear centre trims
Remove the seat belt anchor bolts and the rear quarter trim panels
Remove the upper part of the weatherstrip and the rear header pads
Remove the listing wires and the top ceiling
Warm the new top ceiling
Insert both ends of each listing wire in its place, beginning from the centre
Fit the rear end of the top ceiling to the body flange and its front end into the body's inserting point
how: As the page's figures show; they were not read.

do: Put double-sided adhesive tape on the outside of the body flange
Pull the top ceiling from both sides to take out the slack and glue both sides to the body flange
Clip off every protruding edge and refit the trims in the reverse order
Raise the headlight with the retractor switch
how: If it will not rise, disconnect the battery's negative cable, remove the cover and turn the manual control knob on the retractor motor's shaft until the headlight is fully up.

do: Disconnect the battery's negative cable
Remove the headlight bezel
Loosen the retaining ring's screws, turn the ring counter-clockwise and take it off while holding the headlight
Draw the headlight out and disconnect its connector
Fit the new headlight in the reverse order
Aim the headlights with the two adjusting screws
how: The tyres evenly at their pressure, the car on level ground with no load.
expect: Aimed to the regulation in force.

do: Remove the headlight
Remove the headlight lid
Unhook the spring from the headlight mounting ring and take the ring out
Disconnect the link from the hinge assembly
Remove the hinge's mounting nut and take the hinge assembly out
Fit the new hinge in the reverse order
how: The link is pinched onto its ball pivot with the fingers until it clicks.
caution: Not with pliers.

do: Make the lid's up and down adjustment
Open the hood and raise the headlight
Remove the headlight bezel and disconnect the motor's connector
Disconnect the link from the headlight hinge assembly
Remove the retractor motor and linkage assembly; take it apart if necessary
Fit the motor and linkage in the reverse order
To adjust the lid, with the headlight raised disconnect the link from the hinge assembly
Loosen the lock nut, turn the adjusting screw in or out until the lid sits properly, and tighten the lock nut
Turn the manual control knob until the motor's link is at its lowest, the automatic stop position
Loosen the motor's mounting bolts and nuts and connect the link to the hinge assembly
how: Pinched onto the ball pivot with the fingers until it clicks.
caution: Not with pliers.

do: Move the motor forward or back until the lid is right, then tighten its bolts and nuts
expect: The headlight wiring is clipped in place.

do: With the wipers running, disconnect the battery's negative cable so the blades stop in the upper position
Remove the wiper arms
Remove the seal caps and the nuts on the wiper linkage shafts
Remove the cup washers and the outer bushes
Remove the cowl plate's screws, disconnect the washer hose at the nozzle and take the cowl plate out
Disconnect the wiring connectors at the wiper motor
Remove the wiper motor and link assembly
Refit in the reverse order
Remove the wiper arms, the interior mirror, the front pillar trims and the garnishes
Tape the body, slip a protector in and lift the mould off with the mould remover
Drill a small hole through the sealant and pass a piano wire through it
Wind each end of the wire round a bar and saw through the sealant all round the glass, then lift the glass out
how: Long strokes, so the wear is spread along the wire.
caution: Keep the wire off the paint.

do: Cut the old sealant back with a sharp knife, leaving a thin layer all round the frame
how: SP-1267. Where it has all come off: degrease, prime, let the primer dry (SP-1268) and build the layer up, SP-1712.

do: Bond the new dam to the glass, straight, with its lip outermost
how: Set back from the glass edge by SP-1269.

do: Prime the bonding areas of the body and the glass thinly and let the primer dry
caution: Keep dust off the primer and do not touch it.

do: Bond the spacers to the body and fit the moulding clips, replacing any defective one
how: The spacers' places are in the page's figure; it was not read.

do: Cut the sealant gun's nozzle with a flange to run along the glass edge and a V for the sealant, and lay a smooth ridge round the whole glass between the dam and the edge
how: Ridge height SP-1270. Reshape it with a spatula where needed.

do: Open a door window, lift the glass into place and press it lightly toward the car
caution: A closed car pushes the glass out by air pressure when a door shuts.

do: Smooth away sealant that oozes out and add sealant where the contact is poor
Leave the glass undisturbed while the sealant hardens
Check again for any poorly sealed place and put it right
Clip the mould in and refit the interior mirror, the pillar trims and the garnishes
Remove the garnish and the glass plate's attaching screw
Open the rear glass hatch and disconnect the electrical connector at the rear pillar
Remove the rear pillar trims and the glass's attaching nut
Disconnect the damper stay's end from the rear pillar and hold the hatch up
Cut the glass out with the piano wire
Prepare the frame, bond the new dam to the glass, prime the body and the glass and bond the spacers to the glass
how: As PR-153 steps 5 to 8; the dam's, the primer's and the spacers' places are in the page's figures, which were not read.

do: Lay the sealant round the whole glass, fit the glass and let the sealant harden
Fit the glass's attaching nut, the centre pillar trim and the rear side pillar trim
Connect the damper stay's end to the body, fit the glass plate's screw and the garnish
Disconnect the battery negative terminal
Remove the steering column covers
Unplug the ignition switch's connectors and check the continuity of its terminals in each key position
how: Ohmmeter on the switch side, probe from the harness side of a connector. The 1985 switch's terminal letters: SP-543 to SP-546; S-001 holds this car's wiring.
expect: Continuity exactly as the table; otherwise a new switch.

do: Loosen the switch's attaching screw and take the switch off the key cylinder
Fit the new switch in the reverse order
Test the speedometer on a speedometer tester
how: Read it at each standard speed: SP-434 to SP-437. Tyre wear and wrong tyre pressure add to the error.
expect: Within the allowable range; the odometer counts.

do: Watch the speedometer for needle fluctuation and listen for noise
how: If it fluctuates badly or does not move, take off the speedometer cable: a good cable means a new speedometer.

do: Connect a tachometer to the ignition coil's negative terminal and start the engine
Compare the tester with the car's tachometer
expect: Within the allowable range; otherwise a new tachometer.
caution: Do not drop or knock the tachometer when it is out.

do: Connect a voltage tester across the battery terminals and start the engine
Compare the tester with the car's voltmeter
expect: Within SP-425; otherwise a new voltmeter.

do: Unplug the sender of the gauge being checked
how: Fuel: the fuel tank unit's connector. Water temperature: the gauge unit's connector. Oil pressure: the oil pressure gauge unit's connector.

do: Connect the checker's red lead to the harness connector and its black lead to body ground
Set the checker to each resistance in turn and switch the ignition on
how: Fuel: SP-1083. Oil pressure: SP-787. Hold each setting at least two minutes before judging.
expect: The needle shows each value within twice the needle's width.

do: Judge where the fault is
how: Readings right: the fault is in the sender (PR-158 for the fuel tank unit and the water temperature unit). Readings wrong: the fault is in the meter.

do: Connect an ohmmeter to the fuel tank unit
Move the unit's arm slowly from E to F and read the resistance
expect: Within the range at each point; otherwise a new unit.

do: Remove the water temperature gauge unit
Stand the unit in a container of water and heat the water to 80 C
Measure the unit's resistance
expect: Within the figure; otherwise a new unit.

do: Disconnect the battery cables
Remove the horn cap and the steering wheel
Remove the column covers, the combination switch and the cluster switches
Remove the meter hood and take out the combination meter
how: Press each connector's retaining clip to unplug it from the meter.

do: Strip the meter in order
how: Front lens, plate, voltmeter and oil pressure gauge, tachometer, speedometer, fuel and water temperature gauge, warning lights lens, meter case, printed plate, bulbs and sockets.

do: Check the printed circuit board
how: Look for damage or rust, then check continuity between each connector terminal and its warning light with an ohmmeter.
expect: No damage, rust or open track.

do: Assemble and refit in the reverse order
Release the parking brake fully and unplug the brake fluid level sensor
Jump the sensor's harness terminal to the ground terminal and start the engine
how: SP-389 (1985 wire colours BR and B; S-001 holds this car's).
expect: BRAKE lights.

do: If it does not light, check the fuse, the bulb and the harness
Connect an ohmmeter across the sensor's terminals and move the float up and down
expect: Continuity with the float below MIN, none above MAX; otherwise a new sensor.

do: Unplug the coolant level sensor and start the engine
expect: The coolant level light comes on within SP-771 of starting.

do: If it does not light, check the fuse, the bulb, the sensor unit and the harness
Check the sensor: take it out of the radiator, plug it back in and start the engine with it clear of the body
expect: The light comes on.

do: Ground the sensor's threaded part
expect: The light stays on; otherwise a new sensor.

do: Remove the coolant level sensor unit and wire it to a battery with a test bulb and a switch
Close the switch, then open it
expect: The bulb stays out with the switch closed and lights SP-771 after it opens; otherwise a new unit.

do: Unplug the driver's seat belt buckle switch
Ground the harness terminal and start the engine
how: 1985 wire colour Br; S-001 holds this car's.
expect: BELT lights for SP-408.

do: If it does not light, check the fuse, the bulb, the central processing unit and the harness
Check the buckle switch with an ohmmeter, belt latched and unlatched
expect: As the two rows; otherwise a new switch.

do: Unplug the stop light checker and ground the harness terminal (GL in 1985)
Start the engine
expect: STOP LIGHT warning lights.

do: With the engine running, check for voltage on the checker connector's GL wire, and on its W wire with the brake pedal pressed
expect: Voltage on both.

do: Check continuity from the checker connector's B wire to body ground
expect: Continuity.

do: With both good, unplug either rear combination lamp's 6-pin connector
expect: The stop light warning lights; otherwise a new checker.

do: Unplug the choke and check relay's 4-pin connector and ground its YL terminal (1985 colour)
Start the engine
expect: The charge warning light lights.

do: Wire the relay to a battery through a switch with an ohmmeter on each contact
Switch the coil to battery negative, then to battery positive
how: Each ohmmeter changes, one to continuity and one to none, as the coil is switched.
expect: Both change; otherwise a new relay.

do: Unplug the oil level sensor, ground its harness terminal and start the engine
expect: OIL LEVEL lights; if not, check the fuse, the bulb and the harness.

do: Check the oil level sensor with an ohmmeter while moving its float
expect: No continuity with the float up, continuity with it down; otherwise a new sensor.

do: Unplug the washer fluid level sensor, jump its harness terminal to ground and start the engine
how: 1985 colours LB and B; S-001 holds this car's.
expect: WASHER lights; if not, check the fuse, the bulb and the harness.

do: Connect the washer fluid level sensor to a tester and move its float up and down
expect: Continuity with the float at its lowest.

do: Unplug the fuel tank unit, ground its YL terminal (1985 colour) and start the engine
expect: FUEL lights; if not, check the fuse, the warning light and the harness.

do: If neither the light switch nor the retractor switch works the headlights, check the retractor fusible link
With the link good, read the voltage on the retractor motor connector's R wire with either switch at UP
expect: Battery voltage: the motor's ground or the motor is at fault. None: the wiring, the cluster switch or the light switch.

do: If the retractor switch works them but the light switch does not, read the R wire of the 6-pin connector with the light switch at headlights
expect: Battery voltage: the wiring is at fault. None: check the light switch.

do: If the light switch works them but the retractor switch does not, check the cluster switch's feeds: WG with the switch at UP, RY at DOWN
expect: Voltage on both.

do: With the feeds good, check the outputs: R at UP, RY at DOWN
expect: Voltage on both: the wiring to the motor is at fault. Either missing: a new cluster switch.

do: If the headlights rise but will not lower, check the fusible links and fuses
how: A blown one points to a short between the light switch's RG line and the tail, side marker or illumination lights. None blown: the light switch, the retractor switch or the wiring.

do: If no headlight lights, check the fusible links
Read the headlight connector's RY and RL lines with the light switch on
expect: Battery voltage: the headlamp or its ground is at fault. None: check the light switch.

do: If no tail light lights, check the fusible link and the fuse
Read the light switch connector's RG line with the switch at tail
how: SP-678; the 1985 path continues through X-06, SP-637.
expect: None: check the light switch. Voltage: poor contact at the front-to-rear harness connector.

do: If the stop lights do not light, check the fuse
Test-light the stop light switch connector's W line to ground with the pedal pressed
expect: Lights. If not, test the GW line: lit there means the switch is faulty or misadjusted (pedal height SP-596).

do: If W lit, test-light the stop light checker connector's G line with the pedal pressed
expect: Lit: the stop lamps' ground is at fault. Not lit: the checker.

do: If the instrument illumination does not light, read the panel light control connector's RL line with the light switch at tail
expect: Voltage: the illumination lights' ground is at fault. None: read the RG line - voltage there means the panel light control is faulty.

do: Wire the panel light control to a battery and a test bulb and turn its knob
expect: The bulb dims and brightens; otherwise a new control.

do: If no turn signal works, check the fusible link and the fuse
Ignition on, turn switch on: read the central processing unit's GW line
expect: Battery voltage; none means the hazard switch is at fault.

do: With GW live, probe the unit's GB line
expect: A flashing signal; none means the unit or its ground (SP-405).

do: With the unit good, probe the turn switch connector's GB line with the switch on
expect: Flashing: check the turn switch.

do: If the signals work one way only, check the turn switch and that side's lamp grounds
If turn signals work but hazards do not, check the hazard fuse and probe the cluster switch connector's GB line with the hazard switch on
expect: No flashing: check the GB line from the unit to the switch. Flashing: check the hazard switch.

do: If neither works, check the METER, BACK fuse, then read the cluster switch's LY and GY lines with the ignition on
expect: None: the wiring from the fuse. Voltage: read GW - none means the hazard switch, voltage means the flasher in the unit or the unit's ground (SP-405).

do: If the back-up lights do not light, check the METER, BACK fuse and test-light the rear combination lamp connector's RW line, ignition on, in reverse
expect: Lit: the lamps' ground. Not lit: the back-up switch and the wiring.

do: If only one of the two lights works, check the dead one's bulb and its connector
If neither lights, check the fuse, then jump the central processing unit connector's W line to ground
expect: Both light: the door handle switch or the door-to-front harness contact is at fault.

do: If neither lights with W grounded, read the LY and GL lines
expect: None: the wiring. Voltage: the unit or its ground (SP-405).

do: Unplug the door lock cylinder light and the handle switch and put an ohmmeter on the switch
Work the outer handle
expect: The switch makes and breaks; otherwise a new switch.

do: Check the defroster switch with an ohmmeter
expect: Continuity pressed on, none off; otherwise a new switch.

do: Switch the defroster on and put the voltmeter's positive lead on the middle of each grid line, negative to the body
expect: About SP-397. Higher: the break is on the negative side. Low or nothing: between the middle and the positive side.

do: Clean the broken part of the line
caution: Never petrol or other solvents.

do: Mask both sides of the break, leaving the line exposed
Paint across the break with a fine brush or drafting pen
Let it dry completely
caution: Do not switch the defroster on until the paint is fully dry.

do: Unplug the power window switch and read its BL line, ignition on
expect: Battery voltage; none means the fuse or the harness (SP-482).

do: Check the switch connector's B line to body ground
expect: Continuity.

do: Check the continuity of each switch terminal at UP, OFF and DOWN
how: The table on p.15-37 (not read: the OCR text scrambled it).
expect: As the table; otherwise a new switch.

do: Unplug the window motor and put battery voltage straight on its connector, then reverse it
expect: The glass rises one way and lowers the other; otherwise a new motor.
caution: Do not short the leads to the body, and keep hands out of the door.

do: Unplug the fuel-door release switch and read its LR line to ground
expect: Battery voltage; none means the fuse or the harness.

do: Check the switch with an ohmmeter
expect: Continuity pulled on, none off; otherwise a new switch.

do: Wire the solenoid straight to a battery
expect: It works; otherwise a new solenoid.

do: Unplug the glass hatch release switch and read its LR line to ground
expect: Battery voltage; none means the fuse or the harness.

do: Check the switch with an ohmmeter
expect: Continuity pressed on, none off; otherwise a new switch.

do: Wire the solenoid straight to a battery
expect: It works; otherwise a new solenoid.

do: Unplug the mirror and check continuity between the terminals of its connector
expect: As the row; otherwise a new mirror.

do: Unplug the mirror switch and check continuity in each position, left and right mirror selected
expect: As the rows; otherwise a new switch.

do: Unplug the wiper motor and read its L line, ignition on
expect: Battery voltage; none means the fuse or the harness.

do: Check the motor connector's B line to body ground
expect: Continuity.

do: Put battery positive on motor terminal A and negative on B
expect: The motor runs at low speed.

do: Move the negative lead to terminal C
expect: The motor runs at high speed.

do: Ground the central processing unit's LO line and switch the ignition on
expect: The wipers run intermittently.

do: If they do not, read the unit's L and LW lines
expect: 12 V: check the unit's ground or the wiper motor. None: a new unit.

do: Read the washer motor's L line, ignition on
expect: Battery voltage; none means the fuse or the harness.

do: Ground the washer motor's LY line
expect: The motor runs; otherwise a new washer motor.

do: Read the rear wiper motor's L line, ignition on
expect: Battery voltage; none means the fuse or the harness.

do: Put battery positive on motor terminal A and negative on B and C
expect: The motor turns.

do: Check the rear wiper switch's continuity in each position
expect: As the table; otherwise a new switch.

do: Read the rear washer motor's LB line, ignition on
expect: Battery voltage; none means the fuse or the harness.

do: Ground the rear washer motor's L line
expect: The motor runs; otherwise a new washer motor.

do: Switch off the ignition and the main switch, unplug the control unit's connector and plug it into the ACC checker
Check the actuator inner cable's play, pressing it lightly, and set it with the adjusting nut
Work through check items 1 to 7 of the check table with the ignition and main switch on
how: Main switch, inhibitor switch, brake switch, clutch switch, then SET, COAST and RESUME of the combination switch.
expect: Each check light as the table; a wrong light names the switch and harness to check.

do: Start the engine with the lever at N
Set the slide switch to H and hold the check switch on
expect: Engine speed rises to SP-484 and holds; if not, the actuator, its cable play or its harness.
caution: Release the check switch at once if the engine passes 4000 rpm.

do: At idle, drive the car slowly
expect: The GENERATOR light flashes; if not, the speed sensor or its harness.

do: Measure the actuator solenoid's resistances
expect: Within the figure.

do: If every check passes and the system still misbehaves, fit a new control unit
Unplug the overdrive cancel solenoid and read its B line, ignition on
expect: Battery voltage; none means the fuse or the harness.

do: Put 12 V on the cancel solenoid
expect: Its oil passage closes with current and opens without.

do: Unplug the overdrive switch and read its GY line, ignition on
expect: Battery voltage; none means the fuse or the harness.

do: Check the overdrive switch with an ohmmeter
expect: Continuity off, none pressed on; otherwise a new switch.

do: Press the 4-3 and kick-down switch's plunger and check its two contacts
expect: Each makes at its travel.

do: Hold the accelerator fully down, run the switch's stopper to touch the pedal and lock it with the lock nut
Put 12 V on the kick-down solenoid
expect: It clicks.

do: Wire the kick-down relay to a battery with an ohmmeter on its contact, then take the leads off
expect: Continuity with the coil fed, none without; otherwise a new relay (it is the same part as the stop light check relay).

do: Check the transmission oil pressure switch with air pressure
Wire a voltmeter to the A/T control unit's speed sensor terminal, start the engine and drive slowly at idle
expect: The reading alternates between about 0 and 12 V.

do: Key at ACC, aerial fully out, volume full up, power on
expect: A pop from the speakers.

do: If there is no pop and no hiss, check the radio fuse, then the supply voltage at the unit
expect: Fuse blown: renew it and find the short. Supply good: a faulty unit. No supply: the harness.

do: If it pops but gives no station, check the aerial and its feeder with an ohmmeter
expect: Feeder good; otherwise a new aerial.

do: Check each speaker: meter between the same channel's + and -
expect: The meter reads the speaker's rated impedance and the speaker clicks; otherwise a new speaker.

do: With speakers good, check the harness from the radio to the speakers for shorts and opens
expect: Harness good: a faulty unit.

do: To set the AM trimmer: aerial fully out, key at ACC, radio on AM
Tune a distant weak station, or static if there is none
Turn the trimmer screw left and right to the loudest point
how: A screwdriver through the trimmer hole.
expect: Sensitivity peaks. No change means the station is too strong, or the aerial or its wire is faulty.

do: If the antenna will not move, check the radio or antenna fuse
Unplug the antenna and read the harness side with the key at ACC, radio on and then off
expect: L live with the radio on, R live with it off; otherwise a new antenna relay.

do: Feed the antenna motor straight from a battery each way
expect: The mast goes up and down.

do: Check the relay's continuity
expect: As the rows; otherwise a new relay. All good and still dead: the harness or the radio.

do: To remove it, take off the right rear trunk side trim, unplug the feeder and connector and remove the nuts
Remove antenna bracket No.2 and the drive mechanism cover, then the 4 screws of the drive mechanism
Open the drive mechanism's notch where the cable is fixed and pull the cable out
Loosen the band screw and separate the motor drive unit from the pole
Fit the band under the pole, feed the cable into the motor drive unit and clamp the pole to it with the band
Push the cable tip through the drive mechanism's notch to its stopper and rivet it there with a punch
Screw the drive mechanism together and pull the pole fully out by hand
Turn the drive mechanism left until the cable has no play and engage it with the motor drive gear
Fit the cover and bracket No.2, mount the antenna, connect it, check it works and refit the trim
Check the blower switch's continuity in each position
how: The table on p.15-85 (not read: the OCR text scrambled it).
expect: As the table; otherwise a new switch.

do: Check the blower's B line to body ground
expect: Continuity.

do: Unplug the blower resistor and read its LW line, ignition on
expect: Battery voltage; none means the HEATER fuse, the blower motor or the harness.

do: Check continuity between the resistor's terminals a and 1
expect: Continuity; otherwise a new resistor.

do: Set the mode knob to VENT, pull the heater unit's mode lever fully rearward and clamp the wire
Run the blower on its highest speed with the temperature at COLD
expect: No air from the floor outlets.

do: Turn the temperature knob fully left, push the selector lever down to COLD and clamp the wire
expect: The lever runs its full stroke COLD to HOT.

do: Press the fresh-recirculate switch to run the motor and stop its crank at REC
Unclip the door's connecting rod, push the lever fully toward the motor and refit the rod
Check the door and the motor work
expect: The rack stops as the figure on p.15-94.

do: Measure the voltage at the clutch with it switched on
how: Meter across the clutch lead and ground with the A/C called for, so the coil loads the circuit
expect: at least 11.5 V; if less, the fault is in the car's wiring, not the compressor

do: Spin the pulley with the clutch off
how: Turn the rotor pulley by hand, engine off
expect: it spins freely, no wobble, roughness or vibration
caution: keep hands clear of the belt; engine off

do: Measure the air gap
how: Feeler gauges between the armature plate and the rotor face, at several points round it
expect: 0.4-0.8 mm (SP-1017); above 1.3 mm it may not engage, often only once hot - reset the gap with PR-185 and PR-186

do: Measure the field coil's resistance
how: Ohmmeter across the field coil's lead and the compressor body, at room temperature, lead unplugged
expect: 2.8-4.4 ohm for a 12 V coil (SP-1022); outside that the coil has an internal short or break

do: Take off the dust cover
how: Remove its 3 or 6 bolts, and any sheet-metal auxiliary pulley

do: Remove the armature retaining nut
how: Put the spanner's pins in the armature's threaded holes, hold the armature still and undo the nut with the 3/4 in, 19 mm or 14 mm socket

do: Pull off the armature plate
how: Keyed shaft: thread the puller's 3 bolts into the armature and turn the centre screw clockwise until it comes free. Spline shaft: lift it off by hand, with penetrating oil or two flat screwdrivers gently between rotor and plate
expect: the armature off the shaft

do: Keep the shims and key
how: Lift off the bearing dust cover (if any), the shaft key (if any) and the shims, and keep the shims together
expect: the shims set the air gap - refit the same ones first

do: Pull the rotor pulley
how: Remove the rotor snap ring, set the puller jaws in its groove with the shaft protector over the shaft, finger-tighten the thumb screws, then turn the centre bolt clockwise until the pulley is free
caution: the shaft protector must be on, or the puller damages the shaft

do: Remove the field coil
how: Loosen the lead clamp screw (#2 Phillips) and free the lead, undo its connection, remove the field coil snap ring and lift the coil off

do: Fit the field coil
how: The reverse of PR-185 step 6; the protrusion under the coil ring goes into the hole in the front housing, which locates the lead
expect: the coil cannot turn

do: Drive the rotor pulley on
how: Support the compressor at its rear (in a vice, clamp only the mounting ears). Set the rotor square on the housing boss, put the installer ring on the bearing's inner race only, and drive the rotor down against the housing step with the driver and a hammer or press
expect: the hammer's sound changes when it seats
caution: never push on the seal, the pulley or the bearing's outer race; never clamp the body

do: Refit the rotor snap ring and dust cover
how: External snap ring pliers, any bevel facing away from the compressor; tap the bearing dust cover in gently

do: Fit the shims and the armature
how: The original shims first (on a compressor that never had this clutch: try 1.0, 0.5 and 0.1 mm). Keyed shaft: fit the key, align the keyway and drive the armature down until it bottoms on the shims. Spline shaft: align the slot with the locator tooth and press it on by hand
expect: the armature resting on the shims

do: Torque the armature nut
Check the air gap
how: Feeler gauges all round; tap down gently at high spots; if the whole gap is out, take the armature off and change shims
expect: 0.4-0.8 mm, even all round (SP-1017)

do: Refit the dust cover
caution: overtightening the SD-508 dust cover screws pushes the air gap out of specification

do: Drain the old compressor
how: Remove its oil plug and drain into a container; then drain the suction and discharge ports while turning the shaft clockwise only, with a socket on the armature nut
caution: turn clockwise only

do: Measure the oil drained
how: Measure and write down the amount
expect: the amount the new compressor gets

do: Drain the new compressor the same way
how: A service compressor comes with a full factory charge (SP-1007 for the SD-508): drain it as in step 1

do: Put back the measured amount
how: Pour into the new compressor the amount from step 2
caution: a contaminated or dark oil means the system is flushed first and filled to the factory total (SP-996) instead

do: Refit the oil plug
how: Clean, undamaged seal and O-ring; 15-20 N m (the torque table, SP-1012, gives 19.6)
caution: do not cross-thread the plug

do: Prepare the engine
how: Warm it to working temperature and stop it; take off the air cleaner and plug the vacuum hose; fit a tachometer; an automatic is raised at the rear and supported
caution: the A/T checks run with the rear wheels turning in D: the car must be on stands

do: Check the air vent solenoid
how: Touch it and turn the ignition on and off
expect: the solenoid's movement is felt

do: Check the hot start assist motor
how: Start the engine without touching the accelerator
expect: the motor pulls the throttle partly open

do: Check the vacuum control solenoid (orange wire)
how: Testlight on the coloured wire (black is ground). Federal M/T: no power at any speed. A/T: power in P or N below 1100 rpm, none in D. Then rev above 2000 rpm and release
expect: power for a moment as deceleration starts
caution: California M/T cars have none (advance vacuum from the manifold)

do: Check the switching solenoid (gray wire)
how: Testlight on it; rev quickly past 2000 rpm. Then stop, pull the hose from the check valve, restart, pull the vacuum hose from the solenoid's top
expect: power for a moment while accelerating; air flows from the check valve hose
caution: reconnect both hoses with the engine stopped

do: Check the shutter solenoid (yellow wire) and the coasting valve
how: Testlight on it: power at any speed (A/T also in D); rev to 2000 and release; above 1100 rpm on deceleration suction is felt at the coasting valve inlet and power drops. Unplug the yellow coupler and watch the coasting valve rod
expect: the engine shudders or stalls with the coupler off
caution: A/T back to P; reconnect the coupler

do: Check the relief solenoid (blue wire)
how: Testlight on it; raise the speed slowly; then pull the vacuum hose from its top
expect: power for a moment above about 5000 rpm; relief air at the large hose (air cleaner to air control valve) with the hose off

do: Check the purge valve
how: Off its bracket, the large lower hose off; about 2000 rpm
expect: suction at the open port during acceleration

do: Check the air pump
how: Pinch the inlet hose and raise the speed
expect: the hose collapses; if not, the pump or its V-belt (loose or broken)

do: Check the throttle sensor
how: Unplug the brown coupler; two testlights in the black test coupler (LgY and GY wires); idle, then about 3000 rpm and decelerate
expect: power at idle; both lights on together at about 1100 rpm; if not, set it with the sensor's adjusting screw
caution: testlights no more than 3 W

do: Check No.1 anti-afterburn valve
how: Engine stopped, the hose off at the air pump; restart, 3000 rpm, release
expect: a moment of suction at the hose on deceleration
caution: stop the engine to reconnect

do: Check No.2 anti-afterburn valve
how: Pull and refit its vacuum hose
expect: a moment of suction at the small hose (No.2 AAV to air cleaner) on reconnecting

do: Check the dashpot (M/T only)
expect: the rod meets the throttle lever at 3800-4200 rpm (SP-033) and slows the drop to idle; if not, loosen the top lock nut and turn the dashpot body

do: Test the oil level sensor off the car
how: With the oil drained, take the sensor out of the oil pan; ohmmeter across it, float moved up then down
expect: float UP: no continuity; float DOWN: continuity; if not, replace the sensor

do: Refit the sensor and fill the engine with oil
Check the light with the ignition on
expect: the OIL warning light comes on; if not, the bulb, fuse or wiring

do: Check it goes out running
expect: the light goes out

do: Check the circuit by grounding the coupler
how: Engine idling, unplug the sensor and ground the harness side of the coupler
expect: the light comes on

do: Reconnect
expect: the light out at idle

do: Thread the harness through the gasket and base
how: Through the hole in the plastic gasket first, then the base
caution: the order keeps the harness from being pinched

do: Fit the gasket and base to the door
Thread the harness through the stay and fit the stay
how: Harness through the stay, stay to the base with its 2 screws

do: Connect the mirror and tuck the slack
how: Connect the harness to the mirror's; put the extra harness in the space the bulletin shows, clear of the mounting
caution: a pinched wire shorts the mirror motor

do: Fit the mirror and test it
how: Mirror to the stay with 2 screws; work both directions on both mirrors
expect: the mirror moves both ways

do: Mark the steering wheel against the shaft
how: A mark on the wheel and the shaft so the wheel goes back in the same place

do: Take the steering wheel off
how: Remove the retaining nut and pull the wheel with a steering wheel puller
